name: SIGINT
standfirst: Security research and practitioner news, scored for novelty and actionability.
colophon: sigint.wtf — the correct response to most of these CVEs. Scored by machine against a hand-written rubric; ranking is opinion, not fact.

items.title: Detection and Resolution of Periodic Artifacts in OpenDP's Discrete Laplace Sampler
items.dek: OpenDP discrete Laplace sampler contains periodic artifacts from faulty bernoulli_exp1 in rational arithmetic library; exact arithmetic fixes it.

items.title: CVE-2026-102489 — Zammad GmbH Zammad Session Fixation Vulnerability
items.dek: Zammad GmbH Zammad. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 5 October.

items.title: CVE-2026-102490 — Zammad GmbH Zammad Improper Privilege Management Vulnerability
items.dek: Zammad GmbH Zammad. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 5 October.

items.title: Chaining Skills to Hijack LLM Agents
items.dek: APEX constructs adversarial skill chains that hijack LLM agents 74.2% of the time by forging task-progress records across tool handoffs.
items.unproven: Tested on SkillsBench and six models; no evidence this applies to agents with read-only skills, mandatory inter-skill verification, or restricted tool repositories.

items.title: OverAct: Measuring and Mitigating Proactive Over-Authorization in LLM Tool-Calling Agents
items.dek: LLM tool-calling agents routinely over-authorize data access; SelfAudit defense lowers success by 25 percentage points on GPT with zero-shot filtering.
items.unproven: Tested on seven models and eight privacy-sensitive domains; no evidence that over-authorization persists after fine-tuning, multi-step reasoning, or explicit access-control constraints in the agent framework.

items.title: ABSENTIA: Detecting Broken Access Control Vulnerabilities in Web Applications
items.dek: ABSENTIA scaffolds LLM agents to systematically detect broken access control by mapping routes to code and applying invariant falsification across a testable graph.
items.unproven: BAC-Bench limited to 30 advisories across 25 repositories; false-positive rate and coverage completeness on real applications not quantified; language scope narrow.

items.title: AuraForge: Scaling Security Supervision for Training Coding Agents
items.dek: AuraForge synthesizes executable security tests from real repositories to train coding agents; AuraGym provides 679 tasks across Python, JavaScript, TypeScript covering 177 CWEs.
items.unproven: agent security improvement measured only on AuraGym tasks; transfer to code in the wild not demonstrated; task synthesis coverage and false-test rates not quantified.

items.title: CVE-2026-104286 — Fortinet FortiMail Path Traversal Vulnerability
items.dek: Fortinet FortiMail. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 4 October.

items.title: Sapien: A Stateful Policy Engine for Autonomous AI Agents
items.dek: Sapien enforces stateful policies on agent tool calls using regex with predicates and deferred generation, blocking 93–95% of attacks on AgentDojo while preserving utility.
items.unproven: evaluation limited to two benchmarks; real-world task environments not tested; computational overhead of policy synthesis and verification not measured.

items.title: System-Level Optimization Beyond Cryptographic Kernels: An ML-KEM Case Study on Arm Cortex-M7
items.dek: ML-KEM on Arm Cortex-M7 gains up to 74.6% faster encapsulation through memory hierarchy and public-data reuse, beyond arithmetic optimization.
items.unproven: generalization to other microcontrollers or PQC schemes; whether gains hold with compiler-generated code at optimization levels

items.title: The Innocent Courier: Covert Exfiltration Through Legitimate LLM Web Fetching
items.dek: LLMLeak exfiltrates data from local malware by embedding secrets in URLs fetched by LLM web tools, bypassing network restrictions.
items.unproven: Evaluation on unspecified LLM systems; real-world applicability depends on URL-fetching tool availability and web filter behavior; detection and mitigation strategies not addressed.

items.title: PACE: Provenance-Aware Capability Enforcement for Tool-Using LLM Agents
items.dek: PACE mediates tool calls in LLM agents by verifying execution contracts and confining influence paths before action, blocking 62 of 79 attack configurations.
items.unproven: generalization to production agent architectures outside benchmarks untested; overhead and false-positive rates in live systems unknown

items.title: Autonomous OSS Threat Detection via Taxonomy-Aligned LLMs
items.dek: GPT-4 with taxonomy-aligned prompts detects OSS supply chain threats at 97% accuracy across typosquatting, dependency confusion, and CI/CD poisoning.
items.unproven: evaluation uses curated advisory data, not blind real-world scanning; false-positive rates and deployment feasibility in existing SCA tooling pipelines not measured

items.title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
items.dek: 8,504 query-command pairs benchmark LLM translation to real Kali Linux tools with deterministic verification.
items.unproven: whether benchmark findings transfer to proprietary or custom tools; limited to Kali Linux ecosystem

items.title: An exponential separation between entanglement-assisted and unassisted one-way quantum communication
items.dek: Exponential separation shown between one-way quantum communication with and without preenabled entanglement for total Boolean functions.
items.unproven: Physical realizability of the constructed function; relevance to protocols beyond communication complexity bounds.

items.title: Exponential quantum advantages for decoded quantum interferometry in the streaming setting
items.dek: Decoded quantum interferometry solves optimal polynomial intersection in streaming mode with polylogarithmic space and one pass.
items.unproven: demonstrated on synthetic Hermite interpolation task; no evidence this contradicts lattice hardness or moves migration planning timelines

items.title: Walking the Embedding Space: Datastore Extraction from Multimodal RAG
items.dek: ImRAG extracts training data from multimodal RAG systems by embedding attack payloads in images rather than text prompts.
items.unproven: Evaluation on three unspecified real-world systems; generalization to production defenses and detection mechanisms not established.

items.title: The Achilles' Heel of Partial Reconfiguration: Optical Side-Channel Leakage on the 7-Series ICAP
items.dek: Optical side-channel attack recovers plaintext FPGA bitstream data during dynamic reconfiguration on 7-Series devices.
items.unproven: Attack requires specialized equipment (photon emission microscopy, electro-optical probing) and proximity access; no evidence this applies to production deployments or mitigations already in use.

items.title: False Floors: LLM Safety Routing Evaluations Break Under Distribution Shift
items.dek: Safety router benchmarks show inflated performance due to selection bias; honest scoring under distribution shift reveals routing buys little improvement.
items.unproven: Analysis applies to published benchmarks (HELM, AgentDojo); no evidence whether production routers with domain-specific tuning or retraining regimes suffer the same collapse.

items.title: Helol Tunnel: Covert Channel Exploitation of TLS Extensibility & Privacy Features
items.dek: TLS Client Hello packet reordering exploits anti-ossification and privacy features to tunnel data through NGFWs, evading detection by preserving parameter validity.
items.unproven: tested against unspecified NGFW models; no measurement of detection by modern inspection engines; real-world deployment feasibility unclear.

items.title: Is sandboxing sufficient to contain rogue agents?
items.dek: Analysis of whether sandboxing adequately constrains autonomous agent behavior; informs agent governance policy this quarter.
items.unproven: Specific to theoretical sandbox models; no tested agent deployment data or SDLC integration guidance.

items.title: Do Defenses Against LLM Extraction Work Across Attacks? A Lifecycle Benchmark of Black-Box Model Extraction
items.dek: Unified benchmark evaluates six extraction attacks, ten defenses, and two adaptive attacks against LLM APIs, showing defenses do not generalize across attack variants.
items.unproven: limited to text-only API threat model; query budgets and model sizes not representative of production deployments; long-term extraction risks over weeks or months unaddressed.

items.title: Show HN: Pi pod – Run your pi coding agent in sandboxes on your own server
items.dek: Sandboxed execution harness for Pi coding agent on self-hosted infrastructure, avoiding per-token vendor lock-in.
items.unproven: Security properties of the sandbox isolation, scalability beyond the submitter's team, integration with existing SDLC tooling and policy enforcement.

items.title: Local random quantum circuits converge to the Porter-Thomas distribution in polynomial depth
items.dek: Proof that polynomial-depth random quantum circuits converge to Porter-Thomas distribution, settling a longstanding question in random circuit sampling.
items.unproven: Practical impact on quantum advantage demonstrations; whether tighter bounds are achievable; relevance to near-term noisy devices.

items.title: Quantum Advantage for Two-Party Differential Privacy
items.dek: Quantum protocols for two-party differential privacy achieve constant error, separating quantum from classical information theory.
items.unproven: practical implementation feasibility; scaling to real message lengths; quantum hardware constraints
